scope: Current research delta after the v1 broad prose audit; focus on the concrete remaining narrative-extraction/evaluation boundary rather than repeating generic prose taxonomy research.

sources.title: LitVISTA: A Benchmark for Narrative Orchestration in Literary Text
sources.finding: Frontier models struggle to jointly capture narrative function and structure; end-to-end failures are dominated by event-anchor identification and localization.
sources.system_implication: Keep anchor localization as a separately scored first-class extraction task. Do not infer global orchestration authority from fluent prose analysis alone.

sources.title: NarraBench: A Comprehensive Framework for Narrative Benchmarking
sources.finding: A survey of 78 benchmarks estimates only 27% of narrative tasks are well captured; narrative events, style, perspective, and revelation are especially under-evaluated, and subjective/perspectival tasks often lack one correct answer.
sources.system_implication: Retain task-specific metrics, alternative/unresolved states, and human escalation rather than one aggregate narrative score. Explicitly test perspective and revelation/open-question handling.

sources.title: Lost in Stories: Consistency Bugs in Long Story Generation by LLMs
sources.finding: Long-story consistency errors concentrate in factual and temporal dimensions and often appear in the middle of narratives.
sources.system_implication: Source-held-out calibration must include middle-book factual/temporal slices, not only openings/endings or short passages.

sources.title: EventRelBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating Event Relation Understanding in Large Language Models
sources.finding: General-purpose LLMs remain weak on event relation understanding across coreference, temporal, causal, and supersub relations at sentence and document level.
sources.system_implication: Separate event identity/coreference, temporal and causal extraction scores; a model strong on one relation family must not inherit authority on the others.

sources.title: EventFull: Complete and Consistent Event Relation Annotation
sources.finding: Systematic temporal, causal, and coreference annotation is expensive because event-pair space grows quadratically; integrated annotation tooling can improve consistency and agreement.
sources.system_implication: Gold construction should use an explicit unified relation annotation schema and targeted candidate-pair generation rather than pretending exhaustive manual relation labeling is cheap.

sources.title: Suggest-Verify-Revise: A Three-Stage Document-Level Event Causality Identification with Narrative Consistency
sources.finding: Document-level causal identification benefits from explicit verification/revision rather than unverified one-shot extraction.
sources.system_implication: Candidate extraction should remain noncanonical and flow through validation; unsupported causality must be a first-class false-certainty metric.

sources.title: Once upon a Kernel: Extracting Important Events from Narratives
sources.finding: Narratologically grounded kernel events can distinguish story-moving events from less structurally important events.
sources.system_implication: Future orchestration calibration should distinguish event existence from event narrative role/importance; do not collapse detection and function into one label.

sources.title: LitBench: A Benchmark and Dataset for Reliable Evaluation of Creative Writing
sources.finding: The strongest reported off-the-shelf judge reached about 73% agreement with human preferences, while trained reward models reached about 78%, leaving substantial residual disagreement.
sources.system_implication: Automated literary preference remains evidence, not final authority. Preserve TIE/ABSTAIN, evaluator-robustness checks, and human review for taste/intent boundaries.

sources.title: Style over Story: Measuring LLM Narrative Preferences via Structured Selection
sources.finding: Across six LLMs and three instruction types, model narrative selections consistently favored style over event, character, and setting content dimensions.
sources.system_implication: Keep story-function and preservation vetoes separate from surface-style preference. A stylistically attractive candidate cannot win merely because a judge has stable style bias.

sources.title: How Hypocritical Is Your LLM judge? Listener-Speaker Asymmetries in the Pragmatic Competence of Large Language Models
sources.finding: Pragmatic judging and pragmatic generation are weakly aligned; many models perform much better as listeners/judges than as speakers/generators.
sources.system_implication: Do not infer revision-generation competence from evaluator competence or vice versa. Keep generation and judgment independently qualified.

sources.title: Metaphor and Large Language Models: When Surface Features Matter More than Deep Understanding
sources.finding: Metaphor task performance was strongly influenced by lexical overlap and sentence length, cautioning against interpreting benchmark scores as deep figurative understanding.
sources.system_implication: Future metaphor-function qualification needs contextual minimal pairs and preservation/function evidence, not surface novelty detection alone.

sources.title: AI Suggestions Homogenize Writing Toward Western Styles and Diminish Cultural Nuances
sources.finding: Controlled cross-cultural writing experiments found AI suggestions shifted Indian participants toward American/Western writing patterns and reduced cultural distinctions.
sources.system_implication: Keep project-relative voice/cultural preservation and anti-homogenization vetoes; generic fluency or mainstream-style conformity cannot be a monotonic optimization target.

sources.title: AI writing assistants shrink linguistic diversity and blur personal identity
sources.finding: Research summarized across 880,000 texts reports reduced linguistic variation and shifts in inferred author traits as AI writing assistance spreads.
sources.system_implication: Repeated-revision evaluation should monitor baseline-relative identity/diversity drift while avoiding demographic inference or one ideal diversity target.

sources.title: Homogenizing effect of large language models (LLMs) on creative diversity: An empirical comparison of human and ChatGPT writing
sources.publisher: Computers in Human Behavior: Artificial Humans
sources.finding: Across preregistered studies, groups of human essays added semantic diversity faster than GPT-4 outputs; prompt/parameter diversity interventions did not eliminate the gap.
sources.system_implication: Continue measuring baseline-relative diversity/identity drift across repeated revisions rather than assuming prompt variation solves homogenization.

research_conclusion: The v1 architecture direction remains correct. The strongest current 2025-2026 evidence narrows the next unknown further: extraction and anchor localization accuracy, relation-family calibration, ambiguity/perspective preservation, source-held-out long-context robustness, and separation of story-function evidence from model style preferences. It also strengthens the need to keep generation, judging, voice preservation and cultural-diversity safeguards independently governed. No evidence justifies reopening a generic prose-quality taxonomy or weakening author/voice/preservation boundaries.
stop_condition: Do not perform another broad prose literature sweep until a concrete extractor, benchmark result, or implementation boundary exposes a specific missing state/metric or materially newer evidence changes a requirement.
